title: Operation NickelPinch — Initiative Tracking for Prefetch, Adaptive-batching, and Low-bit Quant Pilots
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Run coordinated pilots across prefetch (KV/prefix caching), adaptive batching heuristics, and low-bit quantization profiles to validate unit-cost regressions while preserving 95th%-ile latency and model quality for chat and completions. Scope: two-week field trials per workload slice (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-heavy), instrumentation hooks in Console, and integration test harness in infra-repo. Approach: run AB experiments with canary traffic ramping (5% -> 30%), collect token-level cost, latency p95/p99, RLHF-quality signals on held-out prompt sets, and qualitative review for hallucination/regressions. Trade-offs/constraints: prioritizing latency-sensitive routes for conservative batching; fallback policies to full-precision model variants on failure; quant profiles gated by per-prompt QA thresholds. Success is defined by net unit-cost reduction with <=2% drop in QA for high-value customers or <=1% change for enterprise SLAs.
okrs: O1: Reduce average token cost for hosted-chat by 12% vs baseline by EoQ2
O2: Maintain latency p95 within 10% of baseline across canaries
O3: Produce rollout playbook and SDK knobs for customers by pilot end
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end instrumentation is reporting token-level cost and per-route p95/p99
Field pilot shows sustained cost reduction for at least one workload slice with QA within thresholds
Rollout playbook drafted with canary ramp and automatic fallback rules
Playbook reviewed and approved by Security, Reliability, and ML Research leads
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: quant profiles cause unpredictable token-level failures — Mitigation: gated trials, automatic degradation to FP16/FP32 and alerting
Risk: batching increases tail latency for multi-tenant bursts — Mitigation: conservative batch size caps and traffic shaping policies
Risk: prefix prefetch staleness leads to correctness drift — Mitigation: TTL heuristics and prompt-set regression checks
